# UIAO CI / Pipeline Integration Guide {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note title="What this page covers"}
This page describes how UIAO uses CI — what gates run on every pull request,
what runs on a schedule or manual dispatch, how the three test tiers are
structured, how to run tests locally, and how to use the `uiao` CLI in your
own pipelines. It is the operator complement to the engineering overview in
[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/AGENTS.md).
:::

---

## Workflow inventory

![UIAO CI gate flow from pull request to main. A PR triggers 13 blocking gates including pytest, ruff, mypy, schema-validation, substrate-drift, publication-gap, metadata-validator, sync-canon-check, three derived-table drift checks, link-check, and docs-leak-check. Any single failure blocks merge and the author fixes and pushes again. On merge to main, quarto renders the HTML site and DOCX to GitHub Pages, image-gen rasterizes SVGs to PNG, and release.yml publishes wheel plus SBOM on a tag push. Scheduled workflows run nightly and weekly. Manual dispatch workflows cover Azure SaaS deploy and tier-1 live-tenant adapter tests.](images/ci-pipeline-integration-diagram-01-gate-flow.png){#fig-ci-gate-flow width="100%"}

UIAO runs **33 CI workflows** in `.github/workflows/`. They fall into four
categories:

### Blocking gates (run on every PR)

These must pass before any merge. A single failure blocks the PR.

| Workflow | File | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| Pytest | `pytest.yml` | Full Python test suite (`pip install -e ".[api]"`) |
| Ruff lint | `ruff.yml` | Python style and lint (zero-finding baseline) |
| Mypy type check | `mypy.yml` | Static typing (zero-error baseline) |
| Schema validation | `schema-validation.yml` | All JSON schemas in `src/uiao/schemas/` are valid |
| Substrate drift | `substrate-drift.yml` | `substrate-manifest.yaml` matches on-disk module state |
| Publication gap | `publication-gap.yml` | 0 publishable docs without a published wrapper (174/174 coverage) |
| Metadata validator | `metadata-validator.yml` | Canon frontmatter schema compliance |
| Sync canon check | `sync-canon-check.yml` | Canon sync state is consistent |
| Customer docs status | `customer-docs-status.yml` | `docs/data/customer-docs-status.md` matches regen |
| Document index status | `document-index-status.yml` | `docs/data/document-index.md` matches regen |
| Sitemap drift | `sitemap-drift.yml` | `docs/data/sitemap.md` matches regen |
| Link check | `link-check.yml` | No broken internal links in docs |
| Docs leak check | `docs-leak-check.yml` | No sensitive patterns in committed docs |

### Render and publish (main branch only)

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `quarto.yml` | Push to `main` | Render HTML site + DOCX; deploy to GitHub Pages |
| `release.yml` | Tag push (`v*`) | Build wheel + SBOM; sign with sigstore; publish to GitHub Releases |
| `image-gen.yml` | Push to `main` or dispatch | Rasterize SVG → PNG via `render_svg_images.py` |

::: {.callout-note}
Quarto rendering runs **only on merge to main** — it does not run on PRs.
Do not wait for "Render HTML site" to appear in a PR's check list; it will not.
:::

### Manual dispatch only

| Workflow | When to run | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | Operator-initiated release | Deploy SaaS to Azure (dev/test/prod) |
| `tier1-cyberark.yml` | When CyberArk creds available | Live-tenant CyberArk adapter test |
| `tier1-palo-alto.yml` | When Palo Alto creds available | Live-tenant Palo Alto adapter test |
| `tier1-service-now.yml` | When ServiceNow creds available | Live-tenant ServiceNow adapter test |
| `fedramp-cr26-roundtrip.yml` | Compliance validation | FedRAMP CR26 OSCAL round-trip via oscal-cli |

### Scheduled

| Workflow | Schedule | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `orchestrator-schedule-nightly.yml` | Nightly | Orchestrator smoke run |
| `conmon-aggregate.yml` | Weekly | ConMon evidence aggregation |
| `scubagear-upstream-track.yml` | Weekly | SCuBA upstream drift tracking |

## Test tier architecture

![UIAO three-tier test architecture. Tier-1 live-tenant tests in tests/integration/tier1/ call real vendor APIs and require network; they run on manual dispatch or nightly cron and call pytest.skip when secrets are absent so the suite is always green without credentials. Tier-2 contract fixture tests in tests/fixtures/contract/ validate adapter output schemas against recorded API responses with no network required; they run on every PR as part of the pytest blocking gate. Tier-3 reference deployment tests run quarterly in a live agency environment and produce compliance evidence artifacts coordinated with the agency AO.](images/ci-pipeline-integration-diagram-02-test-tiers.png){#fig-test-tiers width="100%"}

UIAO uses a three-tier test strategy defined in `UIAO_131 §3.1` and
documented in `tests/integration/README.md`.

### Tier-1 — Live-tenant tests

**Location:** `tests/integration/tier1/`
**Trigger:** Manual `workflow_dispatch` (per adapter) or nightly cron once
credentials are wired.
**Network required:** Yes — calls the vendor's commercial cloud or developer
tenant.

Tier-1 tests are the strongest evidence the substrate emits. They call real
APIs against real tenants. Because vendor sandbox access requires signup,
account verification, and (for some adapters) sales engagement, these tests
are **plumbing-first**: the test scaffolding lands in the repo before the
credentials arrive. All tier-1 tests call `pytest.skip()` when their required
environment variables are absent, so `pytest tests/integration/` is always
green without secrets.

### Tier-2 — Contract fixture tests

**Location:** `tests/fixtures/contract/<adapter>/*.yaml` consumed by
`tests/contract/test_<adapter>_contract.py`
**Trigger:** Every PR via `pytest.yml`.
**Network required:** No.

Tier-2 tests validate that the adapter's output schema matches the UIAO
substrate contract. They use recorded API responses as fixtures — no live
calls. This is the gate that runs on every PR.

### Tier-3 — Reference deployment tests

**Location:** Agency tenant; evidence bundle lives outside this repo.
**Trigger:** Quarterly, per agency.
**Network required:** Yes — live agency environment.

Tier-3 is an operational readiness check run against a real deployed
environment. Results feed the compliance evidence bundle, not the CI gate.

## Running tests locally

### Prerequisites

```powershell
# Clone the repo and install dev dependencies
git clone https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao.git C:\src\uiao
cd C:\src\uiao

# Install with all extras for full local test coverage
pip install -e ".[api,dev]"

# Install pre-commit hooks (runs ruff, mypy, schema validation locally)
pre-commit install
```

### Run the full test suite (Tier-2 only — no credentials needed)

```powershell
pytest tests/ -v --ignore=tests/integration/tier1
```

### Run a specific adapter's contract tests

```powershell
pytest tests/contract/test_entra_id_contract.py -v
pytest tests/contract/test_servicenow_contract.py -v
```

### Run the adapter conformance suite

```powershell
# All adapters — validates each adapter declares required fields
pytest tests/conformance/ -v
```

### Run tier-1 tests with credentials

Tier-1 tests read credentials from environment variables. Set them for the
adapter under test, then run:

```powershell
# ServiceNow example
$env:SERVICENOW_INSTANCE_URL = "https://yourinstance.service-now.com"
$env:SERVICENOW_USERNAME     = "admin"
$env:SERVICENOW_PASSWORD     = "..."

pytest tests/integration/tier1/test_servicenow_tier1.py -v -s
```

Required environment variables per adapter are documented in
`tests/integration/README.md`.

### Schema validation locally

```powershell
# Validate all schemas in src/uiao/schemas/
python scripts/validate_schemas.py

# Validate canon frontmatter
python scripts/validate_canon_frontmatter.py

# Check for publication gaps
python scripts/scan_publication_gaps.py
```

### Pre-commit (runs automatically on git commit)

Pre-commit runs ruff, ruff-format, mypy, and schema validation before every
commit. If `ruff-format` reformats a staged file, the commit aborts — stage
the reformatted file and retry:

```powershell
# After a ruff-format abort:
git add <reformatted-file>
git commit -m "your message"
```

## Interpreting CI failures

### Pytest failure

Read the `pytest` job output in the Actions tab. The failure is shown with
the full traceback. Common causes:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ImportError: uiao.api` | `[api]` extra not installed | `pip install -e ".[api]"` |
| `FileNotFoundError` on a schema | Schema path changed | Update the import or path in the failing test |
| `AssertionError` in contract test | Adapter response schema drifted | Update the fixture or the adapter contract |
| `pytest.skip` everywhere | Tier-1 without credentials | Expected — set env vars or run tier-2 only |

### Publication gap failure

The publication-gap gate enforces that **every publishable doc** (canon ADR,
adapter spec, etc.) has a corresponding published `.qmd` wrapper. When it
fails:

```powershell
# See which docs are missing wrappers
python scripts/scan_publication_gaps.py

# The output lists the canon path and the expected wrapper location
```

Create the missing wrapper (or correct the gap in the scanner's allow-list
if the doc is intentionally unpublished).

### Customer-docs drift failure

Three gates diff committed `docs/data/*.md` files against the regen output.
When they fail, regenerate and commit:

```powershell
cd C:\src\uiao
python scripts/generate_customer_docs_status.py --output docs/data/customer-docs-status.md
python scripts/generate_document_index.py       --output docs/data/document-index.md
python scripts/generate_sitemap.py              --output docs/data/sitemap.md

git add docs/data/
git commit -m "chore: regen derived tables"
```

### Substrate drift failure

The substrate-drift gate checks that `substrate-manifest.yaml` (UIAO_200)
matches the on-disk module state. When it fails:

```powershell
# See what drifted
python -m uiao.substrate walk --report

# Update the manifest to match reality (or fix the code that drifted)
```

## Using the `uiao` CLI in pipelines

The `uiao` CLI is available after `pip install -e ".[api]"` (or the
equivalent in your pipeline). Common pipeline usages:

### OrgPath governance pass (dry-run)

```yaml
# GitHub Actions step
- name: Run OrgPath governance pass
  run: |
    uiao orgtree govern --tenant ${{ env.TENANT_ID }} --dry-run
  env:
    UIAO_ENTRA_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.ENTRA_TENANT_ID }}
    UIAO_ENTRA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.ENTRA_CLIENT_ID }}
    UIAO_ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET }}
```

### Codebook validation

```yaml
- name: Validate OrgPath codebook
  run: uiao orgtree validate codebook
```

### Schema validation gate

```yaml
- name: Validate all schemas
  run: python scripts/validate_schemas.py
```

### Evidence bundle generation

```yaml
- name: Generate evidence bundle
  run: |
    uiao evidence bundle --output evidence/bundle-${{ github.run_id }}.json
```

---

## Required secrets for CI

Set these in **GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions** at the
repository level for the non-environment secrets, and in the appropriate
**Environment** for environment-scoped secrets.

### Repository secrets

| Secret | Used by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| *(none required for blocking gates)* | — | Tier-2 tests and schema validation need no secrets |

### Environment secrets (per environment: `saas-dev`, `saas-test`, `saas-prod`)

| Secret | Used by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | OIDC deployer identity |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | Publisher tenant |
| `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | Target subscription |
| `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP` | `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | Target resource group |
| `PG_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `azure-saas-deploy.yml` | Postgres admin password |

### Adapter tier-1 secrets (manual-dispatch workflows)

| Secret | Adapter | Workflow |
|---|---|---|
| `SERVICENOW_INSTANCE_URL`, `SERVICENOW_USERNAME`, `SERVICENOW_PASSWORD` | ServiceNow | `tier1-service-now.yml` |
| `CYBERARK_*` | CyberArk | `tier1-cyberark.yml` |
| `PALO_ALTO_*` | Palo Alto | `tier1-palo-alto.yml` |
